title: introduce-hook-quota-and-init-throttle-for-private-installs
author: Aisha Ramirez
release_notes: Adds configurable hook quotas and an init-job concurrency throttle to the private Helm chart to reduce rollout-induced cluster contention; defaults preserve existing behaviour
description:
Motivation: Private installs (VPC/on-prem) have seen intermittent resource contention during tenant bootstrap and migration waves: dozens of init jobs and migration hooks spike API and storage load after upgrades. This PR introduces a lightweight, chart-driven quota and throttling facility for init/migration hooks plus templated hook wrappers so operators can opt into safe rollout pacing without modifying existing CI/orchestration.

Summary of changes: Introduce two complementary primitives in values.yaml and templates: 1) hookQuota: a declarative per-namespace limit for concurrent hook jobs (defaults to disabled to preserve backward compatibility). When enabled the chart renders a small controllerJob (CronJob-compatible) which acts as a leader-aware admission gate for init hooks. 2) initThrottle: a per-hook annotation + global chart setting to add a coordinated delay/slot allocation for heavy migration/seed jobs. 3) a templated hook wrapper (templates/hook-wrapper.yaml) that standardizes exit codes, idempotency annotations, and integrates with initThrottle slots. 4) values schema updates (values.schema.json) with strict type checks and allowed ranges and documentation.

Why this approach: We considered a full operator but chose a chart-first, opt-in controller to keep air-gapped installs simple. The wrapper is a minimal shim that can be used by existing hooks with a one-line change to the hook Job spec. The controller uses only RBAC and a ConfigMap-backed token ring so it remains lightweight for on-prem clusters.

What changed (high level): commits, templates, and docs. Key templates added: templates/hook-wrapper.yaml, templates/hook-quota-controller-deploy.yaml, templates/hook-quota-rbac.yaml, templates/_helpers.tpl (new helpers for annotations). values.yaml additions and values.schema.json schema expanded. README and docs/upgrade-notes.md updated with migration instructions and examples.

Migration notes and backwards compatibility: Default values keep previous behavior (quota disabled, throttle disabled). To opt-in operators set values.private.hookQuota.enabled: true and configure per-namespace quotas. A migration helper script (scripts/generate-quota-config.sh) is included to derive quotas from cluster capacity metrics free-form; this is provided as an optional utility for large fleets.

Commits (summary):
- Add hook quota controller deployment and RBAC, basic leader lock implementation
- Add hook-wrapper template and helper macros for deterministic annotations
- Expand values.schema.json with hookQuota and initThrottle sections and validation rules
- Add scripts/generate-quota-config.sh helper and README example
- Docs: upgrade-notes and example values for multi-tenant on-prem clusters
- Tests: add helm template smoke and basic rendering unit tests

Changed files (high level):
- values.schema.json (expanded)
- values.yaml (new options + docs)
- templates/hook-wrapper.yaml (new)
- templates/hook-quota-controller-deploy.yaml (new)
- templates/hook-quota-rbac.yaml (new)

Example values snippet (in chart values.yaml):
private:
  hookQuota:
    enabled: false # disable by default, enable to gate init hooks per-namespace
    defaultConcurrent: 5 # max concurrent init hook Jobs per namespace
    namespaceOverrides:
      "tenant-a": 2
  initThrottle:
    enabled: false
    defaultSlotDelaySeconds: 6
    maxStaggerSeconds: 300

Review conversation (high level):
- Jonas Park: Asked for a plan to ensure the controller cannot become a single-point-of-failure. Resolution: added leader election (ConfigMap lock) and a no-op fallback that allows hooks to run after X minutes if controller unresponsive (configurable via hookQuota.unblockAfterSeconds).
- Marta Liu: Requested stricter schema validation for negative numbers and upper bounds. Resolution: added min/max bounds in values.schema.json and unit tests for invalid values.
- Evan Cho: Ran perf-canary with a synthetic tenant wave and reported a 42% reduction in API server QPS spike. Requested a small change to default delays; changed defaultSlotDelaySeconds from 10 -> 6 after discussion.
- CI bot: Initially flagged lint failure for long helper names, fixed by shortening template helper IDs and adding comments.

CI summary: GitHub Actions helm-lint, kubeval, and chart-testing passed after two iterations. Perf-canary job passed on the second run (first run had a flaky cluster provisioning issue unrelated to code).

Rollout and merge: Merged via squash on main. Ops follow-up: perf-canary pipeline will be updated to include the optional e2e scenario that enables private.hookQuota for one canary tenant (refer ENG-8214 follow-up). The feature is gated behind chart values so existing private installs are unaffected until operators opt in.

Notes for operators: See docs/upgrade-notes.md for example values and an FAQ on how to choose defaultConcurrent and unblockAfterSeconds. The helper script is intentionally non-opinionated: run it offline to generate per-namespace suggestions and validate against values.schema.json before applying.
